_comment: THE MUTANTS, COMMITTED, because the alternative is grading my own homework.
A mutation run is only as good as its mutant list, and a list written by the
same person as the tests contains the mutations those tests already catch. On
2026-09-28 that produced a 14/14 score on this package while an independent
reviewer's 54-mutant sweep found 27 survivors -- including a checkpoint that
recorded the newest row instead of the page boundary, which is the defect the
release existed to fix, and a drift gate that still passed with 30 of 36
Committing the list is most of the value: a reviewer can read what is being
checked and, more importantly, what is not. Add a mutant whenever a defect
reaches main -- the mutation is the proof the new test would have caught it.
Each entry replaces `find` with `replace` in `file`, once, then runs the whole
suite. A SURVIVOR is a change to production code that breaks nothing, which
means either the tests are blind to it or the code does not matter.

mutants.name: checkpoint the newest row instead of the page boundary
mutants.why: The defect 4.0.0 exists to fix. An entity that stopped reporting has no rows for the tail days of its page, so a row-derived checkpoint re-downloads days already written.

mutants.name: resume ignores the recorded boundary
mutants.why: The fallback is for state files with no boundary. Preferring it always reintroduces the duplicate.

mutants.name: a resumed run losing its BUDGET deletes the accumulated file
mutants.find:
if progress.written == 0 and not resumed_run:
            # A budget spent before the first page left a 0-byte file that reads
            # as "this park has no history".
            out_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
mutants.why: Exit 75 is the ORDINARY outcome of a long back fill, so this is the more dangerous of the two sites: the file vanishes, the next run appends only the tail and records complete.

mutants.name: a resumed run failing any OTHER way deletes the accumulated file
mutants.find:
if progress.written == 0 and not resumed_run:
            out_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            state_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
mutants.why: `written` counts rows THIS process wrote. On a resumed run the file holds everything the previous runs fetched.

mutants.name: the column fingerprint is ignored
mutants.why: 3.3.0's 19-column file resuming under a 41-column build appends rows no reader can parse.

mutants.name: a state file from the other SDK is accepted
mutants.why: The two SDKs' keys differ only on the interrupted path, so the safe paths interoperate silently and a cross-SDK resume duplicates.

mutants.name: the format leaves the state filename
mutants.why: One state file for two formats doubles every row on an ndjson -> csv -> ndjson round trip.

mutants.name: a unique substring returns the display label as the park name
mutants.replace:
if len(park_hits) == 1:
        return [(pid, f"{pname}  (x)") for pid, pname in park_hits]
mutants.why: Shipped in 3.3.0: parkName read 'Magic Kingdom Park  (Walt Disney World® Resort)' for ~94,000 rows.

mutants.name: normalize becomes a bare casefold
mutants.find:
folded = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", value.casefold())
    return "".join(c for c in folded if c.isalnum() and not unicodedata.combining(c))
mutants.why: Five live park names carry ®, a curly apostrophe or an accent, and the documented example is one of them.

mutants.name: an exact destination no longer beats an exact park
mutants.why: Seven real names are both a destination and one of its several parks. Cedar Point would download one of two.

mutants.name: the CSV writer stops quoting a carriage return
mutants.find: if any(ch in text for ch in ('"', ",", "\r", "\n")):
mutants.replace: if any(ch in text for ch in ('"', ",", "\n")):
mutants.why: Python's csv module did exactly this on 3.9 and 3.10, and one row parsed as two.

mutants.name: the CSV loses its BOM
mutants.why: Excel on Windows then reads the local code page and mangles every ® and accent.

mutants.name: a negative number is prefixed as a formula
mutants.why: Every negative value in the file becomes text and arithmetic breaks in the tool the prefixing protects.

mutants.name: the row renames the run
mutants.why: Models keep undeclared fields, so a row carrying its own entityId would relabel every line of a paid export.

mutants.name: a collection of models is flattened as a nested block
mutants.why: Phantom columns in the header, then AttributeError on the first row, the moment the API adds an array of objects.

mutants.name: a network failure exits 1 instead of 75
mutants.find:
return EX_TEMPFAIL
    except ThemeParksError as exc:
mutants.why: A resumable failure should make a scheduler retry, not alert.

mutants.name: the page hook fires before its rows
mutants.find:
yield from _daily_entity_rows(envelope)
            # AFTER the rows, never before: a caller checkpointing on this has to
            # be able to trust that everything the page held is already written.
            if on_page is not None:
                on_page(_page_of(envelope))
mutants.why: A consumer that died mid-page would record a checkpoint past rows it never wrote. Losing rows is worse than duplicating them.

mutants.name: the entity label comes from somewhere other than the response
mutants.why: `str(EntityType.SHOW)` is 'EntityType.SHOW', so a customer filtering on 'SHOW' matches nothing and is told nothing.

mutants.name: models stop keeping undeclared fields
mutants.why: A stale vendored spec then deletes real data at parse time, which is how unknownMinutes, inParkHours and extremeWaits were lost.

mutants.name: a run ends at retrievable_through again
mutants.why: 4.0.1 ended every run on today, so the newest rows in every file were partial days, and nothing ever replaced them.

mutants.name: final_through ignores recorded_to
mutants.why: The same defect one layer down: the final boundary becomes today again for every caller of span().

mutants.name: a finished park is left alone again
mutants.find: if end is None or continue_at > str(end):
mutants.why: 4.0.1's behaviour: a rerun of a finished park printed that it was complete and exited 0, so a nightly cron never fetched another day.

mutants.name: a finished state written to another contract is appended to
mutants.replace: if mismatch is not None and not state.get("complete"):
mutants.why: Only unfinished mismatched states were refused; a finished one fell through to a fresh start in append mode and doubled the file under a second header.

mutants.name: a state file with no data file is continued
mutants.find:
if state and not file_exists:
        state = {}
mutants.why: Continuing writes a file that starts part-way through its range and records it complete.

mutants.name: a 4.0 file keeps its partial tail
mutants.why: The partial days 4.0 wrote stay in the file for good, next to nothing that would ever correct them.

mutants.name: --since is ignored on a first run
mutants.find: start = _later(rng.since, ask.archive_from) if rng.since is not None else ask.archive_from
mutants.why: The customer asked for a year and got the whole archive, which is the defect --since exists to fix.

mutants.name: a --since that would leave a gap is accepted
mutants.find: if since is not None and str(since) > continue_at:
mutants.why: The file would skip days the state file then claims it holds.

mutants.name: changes() loses a park's openings
mutants.find: return {entity.id: entity.opening for entity in entities}
mutants.why: The opening is the state before the first change; without it a day cannot be rebuilt from raw history.

mutants.name: a continued file jumps to the key's first day
mutants.why: A cron that missed more nights than the key's window carries on from the key's first day, leaving days missing from the middle of a file whose state claims them.

mutants.name: the NDJSON trim drops the cut day itself
mutants.find: if isinstance(day, str) and day > keep_through:
mutants.replace: if isinstance(day, str) and day >= keep_through:
mutants.why: The day at the cut is one the state says the file holds; dropping it leaves a hole.

mutants.name: a 403 at exactly the resume day is reported as a gap
mutants.find: if start is None or floor <= str(start):
mutants.replace: if start is None or floor < str(start):
mutants.why: The key reaches the day the file continues from, so the refusal is an error to surface, not a gap.

mutants.name: the upgraded 4.0 state is not written
mutants.why: A run that stops right after the upgrade leaves a trimmed file under a version-1 state, trimmed again next time.

mutants.name: the upgrade keeps the old lastDay
mutants.find: upgraded["lastDay"] = keep_through if last_day is not None else None
mutants.why: The state would claim a day the trim just removed.

mutants.name: no checkpoint after a page
mutants.why: The defect a review found: an interrupted extension left the old state, and the rerun appended the same days again.

mutants.name: no checkpoint before the first request
mutants.find: progress.checkpoint(job.state, _size(handle), None if start is None else str(start))
mutants.why: An extension killed mid-first-page left `complete: true` with the old end, and the rerun appended those rows twice.

mutants.name: the rerun does not cut back to the checkpoint
mutants.why: Whatever was written after the last checkpoint is appended again after it.

mutants.name: the state file is written in place
mutants.why: A crash or a full disk mid-write leaves half a state file, which reads as none.

mutants.name: a failed trim leaves its scratch copy
mutants.find:
except BaseException:
        scratch.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    return kept
mutants.why: A full disk during a trim leaves a second partial copy of the data file behind.

mutants.name: a legacy state resumes at lastDay again
mutants.why: lastDay is the newest day ANY entity reached; the entities behind it lose the days in between.

mutants.name: the state records the start asked for, not the first day written
mutants.why: After the window clamp, a --since earlier than the real first day passed silently.

mutants.name: the same --since before the file's first day is refused
mutants.why: A cron line with a fixed --since older than the key's window fails every night after the first.

mutants.name: two runs on one park are not locked out
mutants.why: Two runs read the same state and append the same days.

mutants.name: a 4.0 file emptied by the cut is continued, not started again
mutants.find:
if size == 0:
        # Nothing survived the cut
mutants.replace:
if False:
        # Nothing survived the cut
mutants.why: Every anonymous 4.0 file: continued from a day the key can no longer read, and refused on every later run.
